A1.justification: Both PDFs describe M-Attack, with matching authors, methods, and retained experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations against commercial LVLMs, component and hyperparameter ablations, and a 1,000-image comparison in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds open-source model evaluations, captioning and VQA experiments, and diagnostic analyses in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Random local cropping, cosine-similarity matching, the surrogate ensemble, and optimization procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1-3, including the alternative MI-FGSM and PGD-ADAM implementations, are retained. The additional evaluations do not establish a changed attack procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained NIPS 2017 evaluations, v2 adds image captioning with ImageNet source images and COCO2014 validation targets, plus visual question answering on OK-VQA (Appendix G.3, Tables 13-16). These substantially broaden the represented data and task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain AttackVLM, SSA-CWA, AnyAttack, and AdvDiffVLM in Table 2, and AnyAttack in the 1,000-image comparison. Added benchmark comparisons reuse existing attackers; newly evaluated victim models are not new attack baselines.

E3.justification: The original evaluation settings remain stable, but new experiments introduce standard captioning metrics, VQA accuracy with pre-attack controls, and one-, three-, and five-query budgets. v2 also evaluates additional open-source victim models, including Qwen-2.5-VL, LLaVA-1.5, BLIP, BLIP2, and InstructBLIP.

E4.justification: v2 adds KMR validation using semantically similar and different clean-image controls, query-budget sensitivity, and quantitative perturbation-distribution comparisons with and without local cropping (Tables 17-19). Figure 13 and Appendix H.2 add failure cases. The earlier crop, ensemble, optimizer, and step-size ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Standard-deviation shading in the ECDF analysis is retained from v1 Figure 5 as v2 Figure 3. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty or significance tests for attack performance; v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of significance reporting.

E6.justification: Retained table values are unchanged after matching renumbered tables, but Tables 12-19 add substantial results. Examples include ASRs of 0.90 on Qwen-2.5-VL and 0.95 on LLaVA-1.5, and GPT-4o OK-VQA accuracy of 7.8% after M-Attack versus 27.0% before attack. These are newly evaluated settings, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Equation (4) changes the crop-union inequalities from non-strict to strict, altering the formal diversity requirement. Its universal i,j quantifier remains, leaving the i=j case problematic. Appendix B's optimal-transport proposition and proof sketch are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract adds a priority claim that this is the first tight analysis connecting perturbation optimization with semantics. The principal contributions—local matching, ensemble-based transferability, KMRScore, and over 90% success on GPT-4.5/4o/o1—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds an interpretation of global matching's early similarity saturation versus slower local matching. Appendix H.2 identifies crowded, multi-object images as failure conditions for M-Attack, while Appendix G discusses query-efficiency tradeoffs and the new diagnostic findings.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses random source-target pairing, 20 sampled images for the ECDF, temperature zero, and per-image runtime and memory: 20.04 seconds and 549.78 MB on one RTX 4090. It removes the Ubuntu 22.04 specification. Code and dataset links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 positions part of its novelty as analysis of an existing source-target matching strategy. It adds the OK-VQA reference, replaces the cited PyTorch source, and removes several background references while condensing related work. The principal positioning against existing attack methods is retained.

P1.justification: Related Work is extensively rewritten and condensed, and the failed-attack investigation is substantially reorganized. The appendix reorders ablations, implementation, and settings, separates experimental results from visualizations, and gains a contents page. Broader Impacts, Limitations, and a NeurIPS checklist are added.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout, rearranges plot panels in Figures 8-9, and relocates appendix tables beside their discussions. It adds eight result tables and a failure-case figure. Existing heatmaps, perturbation visualizations, and interaction screenshots are largely retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The added captioning and OK-VQA evaluations, diagnostic controls, failure cases, and resource information improve validation and transparency. However, the new protocols are briefly specified, and Table 18's one-query results conflict with Table 2—for example, GPT-4o KMRc is 0.20 versus 0.13. The stronger analysis claim also accompanies an unchanged proof sketch, limiting the overall gain.
